# Question and experimental design

Did soybean aboveground biomass differ among five management systems, and did
system differences vary among experiments (site-years)?

The experiment evaluated five management systems in a split-plot design across
three site-years, with four blocks per site-year (60 subplot observations).
Cereal rye termination method was assigned to whole plots within blocks:
moldboard plowing (tilled) or roller-crimping (rolled). Within tilled whole
plots, subplots received cultivation (TIC) or mowing (TIM). Within rolled whole
plots, subplots received no supplemental weed control (RNO), mowing (RIM), or
high-residue cultivation (RIC). One soybean biomass observation was collected
per subplot. Thus, subplots are the observational units, while comparisons
between systems with different termination methods depend on whole-plot
replication. The five systems are not a fully crossed factorial treatment.

In 2023, an operations error caused one subplot randomized to RNO to receive
RIC (high-residue cultivation). All other treatments were implemented as
assigned. This error did not alter the termination whole plots: TIM and TIC
remained together, and the three rolled-system subplots remained within their
roller-crimped whole plot. The primary analysis retains the original randomized
treatment labels rather than reclassifying the affected subplot. The processed
data retain one record for each randomized treatment per block; the affected
subplot's identity is not independently verified here against a randomization
map. RIC received only one late cultivation event rather than the intended
repeated cultivations, so interpretation concerns the management as implemented.

# Analysis overview

This analysis evaluates aboveground soybean crop biomass (kg/ha) across three
site-years. Management system and its interaction with site-year are included
as fixed effects. The random-effects structure reflects the split-plot
randomization, with termination methods assigned to whole plots and management
systems evaluated at the subplot level. Comparisons between termination methods
must therefore account for whole-plot replication.

Observed means and variability describe the field measurements. Model-based
estimated marginal means, standard errors, and comparisons provide inference
while accounting for the experimental design. Figures using both approaches
are retained for transparent reporting.

# Setup

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = TRUE, warning = TRUE, error = FALSE)
```

```{r packages-and-settings, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(conflicted)
library(WrensBookshelf)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
# multcomp supplies cld(); multcompView supplies its letter-display algorithm.
# nlme is used via explicit namespace calls in the variance sensitivity check.
for (pkg in c("multcomp", "multcompView", "nlme")) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("Required package is not installed: ", pkg)
  }
}

conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter)
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::select)

method_levels <- c("Roller-crimper", "Moldboard plow")
treatment_levels <- c("RNO", "RIM", "RIC", "TIM", "TIC")
treatment_labels <- c(
  RNO = "Rolled,\nno control",
  RIM = "Rolled,\nmowing",
  RIC = "Rolled,\nhigh-residue cultivation",
  TIM = "Tilled,\nmowing",
  TIC = "Tilled,\ncultivation"
)

experiment_labels <- c(
  V_2023 = "2023 – Field V",
  O2E_2024 = "2024 – Field O2 East",
  O2W_2024 = "2024 – Field O2 West"
)

experiment_colors <- setNames(
  WrensBookshelf::WB_brewer(
    name = "WhatWellBuild", n = 5, type = "discrete"
  )[c(1, 3, 5)],
  names(experiment_labels)
)
method_lookup <- c(
  RNO = "Roller-crimper", RIM = "Roller-crimper",
  RIC = "Roller-crimper", TIM = "Moldboard plow",
  TIC = "Moldboard plow"
)

treatment_colors <- setNames(
  WrensBookshelf::WB_brewer(name = "WhatWellBuild", n = 5, type = "discrete"),
  treatment_levels
)

theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 16))
figure_caption_theme <- theme(
  plot.caption = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.1)
)
lsd_caption <- paste(
  "Letters: mixed-model Fisher's LSD comparisons at α = 0.05.",
  "Shared letters indicate no significant difference detected, not statistical equivalence.",
  sep = "\n"
)

# Plain tables render in both HTML and GitHub Markdown.
show_table <- function(x, caption, digits = 1) {
  knitr::kable(x, digits = digits, caption = caption)
}

# Use the same degrees-of-freedom method in ANOVA and estimated means.
emm_options(lmer.df = "satterthwaite")

fmt_biomass <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ",")
fmt_p <- function(x) {
  if (x < 0.001) "< 0.001" else
    paste("=", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3))
}

tab_dir <- here("output", "tables", "soybean_crop_biomass")
dir.create(tab_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```



# Import and validate

The processed dataset is generated separately in `data_prep.Rmd`;
this analysis uses its biomass values in kg/ha without additional conversions.
Checks require one record per treatment in each of four blocks within each
site-year and ensure that the response is finite and nonnegative.

```{r import-and-check}
processed_file <- here("data", "processed", "combined_processed.rds")
processed_data <- readRDS(processed_file)
# Identify the exact input without repeating preparation or unit conversions.
show_table(
  tibble(input = "data/processed/combined_processed.rds",
         MD5 = unname(tools::md5sum(processed_file))),
  "Processed-data provenance"
)

required <- c(
  "site_year", "block", "treatment", "bean_biomass_kg_ha"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(required, names(processed_data))

if (length(missing_columns)) {
  stop("Missing columns: ", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "))
}

plot_data <- processed_data |>
  select(all_of(required)) |>
  mutate(across(c(site_year, block, treatment), as.character))

if (anyNA(plot_data[c("site_year", "block", "treatment")]) ||
    any(vapply(
      plot_data[c("site_year", "block", "treatment")],
      function(x) any(trimws(x) == ""),
      logical(1)
    ))) {
  stop("Missing or blank site-year, block, or treatment identifiers.")
}

if (!setequal(unique(plot_data$site_year), names(experiment_labels))) {
  stop("Site-year identifiers do not match experiment_labels.")
}

if (!setequal(unique(plot_data$treatment), treatment_levels)) {
  stop("Treatment identifiers do not match treatment_levels.")
}

y <- plot_data$bean_biomass_kg_ha

if (!is.numeric(y) || any(!is.finite(y)) || any(y < 0)) {
  stop("Biomass must contain finite, nonnegative numeric values with no missing data.")
}

plot_counts <- plot_data |>
  count(site_year, block, treatment)

block_counts <- plot_counts |>
  count(site_year, block, name = "n_treatments")

experiment_counts <- block_counts |>
  count(site_year, name = "n_blocks")

if (any(plot_counts$n != 1L) ||
    any(block_counts$n_treatments != 5L) ||
    any(experiment_counts$n_blocks != 4L)) {
  stop(
    "Expected one record per treatment, five treatments per block, ",
    "and four blocks per site-year."
  )
}

plot_data <- plot_data |>
  mutate(
    site_year = factor(site_year, levels = names(experiment_labels)),
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = treatment_levels),
    primary_method = factor(
      unname(method_lookup[as.character(treatment)]),
      levels = method_levels
    ),
    block_id = interaction(site_year, block, drop = TRUE),
    whole_plot_id = interaction(
      block_id, primary_method, drop = TRUE
    )
  )

validation_summary <- plot_data |>
  group_by(site_year) |>
  summarise(
    plots = n(),
    blocks = n_distinct(block_id),
    whole_plots = n_distinct(whole_plot_id),
    min_biomass = min(bean_biomass_kg_ha),
    max_biomass = max(bean_biomass_kg_ha),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

show_table(
  validation_summary,
  "Validated records and soybean biomass range (kg/ha)"
)
```



# Prepare subplot observations

Each subplot contributes one biomass observation, so no within-subplot
averaging is needed. Sum contrasts support Type III fixed-effect tests in the
model containing the management-system-by-site-year interaction.

```{r prepare-subplots}
biomass_data <- plot_data

contrasts(biomass_data$treatment) <- contr.sum(5)
contrasts(biomass_data$site_year) <- contr.sum(3)
```

# Describe the observations

The table summarizes observed means and standard deviations for each
management system within each site-year. Standard deviations describe
variation among the four subplot measurements and are not model-based
standard errors.

```{r observed-summary}
biomass_summary <- biomass_data |>
  group_by(site_year, treatment) |>
  summarise(
    n_plots = n(),
    mean_biomass = mean(bean_biomass_kg_ha),
    sd_biomass = sd(bean_biomass_kg_ha),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

show_table(
  biomass_summary,
  "Observed subplot soybean biomass: mean and SD (kg/ha)"
)
```
The exploratory figure displays individual observations and arithmetic
means. It helps reveal site-year differences and differences in observed
spread before fitting the mixed model.

```{r observed-figure, fig.width=11, fig.height=5}
ggplot(biomass_data, aes(treatment, bean_biomass_kg_ha)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = treatment),
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, seed = 123),
    size = 2.5,
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    shape = 18,
    size = 4,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~site_year,
    labeller = labeller(site_year = experiment_labels)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = treatment_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    x = "Management system",
    y = "Soybean crop biomass (kg/ha)",
    caption = paste(
      "Colored points are subplot observations;",
      "black diamonds are treatment means."
    )
  ) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0)
  )
```

# Fit the primary model

The initial model includes block and termination whole-plot random intercepts.
Management system and site-year, including their interaction, are fixed effects.
The interaction is retained so that comparisons can be estimated separately by
site-year or averaged equally across site-years, regardless of the interaction
p-value. Site-year is fixed, so inference describes these three observed
experiments. Unique block IDs nest blocks within site-years, and whole-plot
IDs nest termination whole plots within blocks. A whole-plot intercept models
correlation among its subplots. With one observation per subplot, a separate
subplot intercept cannot be distinguished from residual error. The model
assumes homogeneous residual variance.

```{r fit-model}
biomass_model_full <- lmerTest::lmer(
  bean_biomass_kg_ha ~ treatment * site_year +
    (1 | block_id) + (1 | whole_plot_id),
  data = biomass_data,
  REML = TRUE
)
```

# Evaluate random-effects structure

The initial model estimated the additional block-level variance at zero and
reported a singular fit. We retain it for documentation and fit a simpler
model with the whole-plot intercept. The latter preserves within-whole-plot
correlation and is used for the subsequent analysis. Singularity alone does
not establish a treatment effect or its absence.

```{r full-model-variance}
show_table(
  as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(biomass_model_full)) |>
    transmute(component = grp, variance = vcov, SD = sdcor),
  "Variance components for initial biomass model", digits = 1
)
cat("Initial model singular:", lme4::isSingular(biomass_model_full), "\n")
```

```{r simplified-model-check}
biomass_model <- lmerTest::lmer(
  bean_biomass_kg_ha ~ treatment * site_year +
    (1 | whole_plot_id),
  data = biomass_data,
  REML = TRUE
)

cat(
  "Biomass model singular:",
  lme4::isSingular(biomass_model, tol = 1e-4),
  "\n"
)
```

# Sensitivity to the random-effects structure

The initial model includes a block intercept whose estimated variance was zero.
To check whether omitting it changes inference, compare the treatment estimated
marginal means and their SEs from both models, averaging site-years equally.
We also compare all pairwise treatment contrasts. This is a sensitivity check,
not a new model-selection test. Subsequent results continue to use the simpler
`biomass_model`.

```{r random-structure-sensitivity}
full_emm <- emmeans(biomass_model_full, ~ treatment, weights = "equal")
simple_emm <- emmeans(biomass_model, ~ treatment, weights = "equal")

sensitivity_means <- as.data.frame(summary(full_emm)) |>
  select(treatment, full_mean = emmean, full_SE = SE, full_df = df) |>
  left_join(
    as.data.frame(summary(simple_emm)) |>
      select(treatment, simple_mean = emmean, simple_SE = SE, simple_df = df),
    by = "treatment"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    mean_difference = simple_mean - full_mean,
    SE_difference = simple_SE - full_SE
  )

show_table(
  sensitivity_means,
  "Treatment EMM sensitivity to the random-effects structure (kg/ha)",
  digits = 2
)

full_pairs <- as.data.frame(summary(pairs(full_emm, adjust = "none"))) |>
  select(contrast, full_estimate = estimate, full_SE = SE,
         full_df = df, full_p = p.value)
simple_pairs <- as.data.frame(summary(pairs(simple_emm, adjust = "none"))) |>
  select(contrast, simple_estimate = estimate, simple_SE = SE,
         simple_df = df, simple_p = p.value)

sensitivity_pairs <- full_pairs |>
  left_join(simple_pairs, by = "contrast") |>
  mutate(
    estimate_difference = simple_estimate - full_estimate,
    SE_difference = simple_SE - full_SE
  )

show_table(
  sensitivity_pairs,
  "Pairwise treatment-contrast sensitivity (kg/ha; unadjusted p-values)",
  digits = 4
)

# Compare both reporting procedures, using the same families in each model.
sensitivity_decisions <- tibble(
  procedure = c("Fisher's LSD (unadjusted)", "Tukey (ten comparisons)"),
  changed_decisions = vapply(c("none", "tukey"), function(adjustment) {
    full_p <- as.data.frame(summary(pairs(full_emm, adjust = adjustment)))$p.value
    simple_p <- as.data.frame(summary(pairs(simple_emm, adjust = adjustment)))$p.value
    sum((full_p < 0.05) != (simple_p < 0.05))
  }, integer(1))
)
show_table(sensitivity_decisions, "Changes in pairwise decisions at α = 0.05", digits = 0)
```

The initial model's estimated block variance was
`r formatC(as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(biomass_model_full))$vcov[as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(biomass_model_full))$grp == "block_id"], format = "f", digits = 1)`.
Dropping that intercept changes pooled treatment means by at most
`r formatC(max(abs(sensitivity_means$mean_difference)), format = "e", digits = 2)` kg/ha
and pairwise contrast SEs by at most
`r formatC(max(abs(sensitivity_pairs$SE_difference)), format = "e", digits = 2)` kg/ha.
There are `r sum(sensitivity_decisions$changed_decisions)` changed decisions across
the two comparison procedures. These checks assess numerical stability, not
whether blocking was unnecessary in the design. EMMs are compared using means,
SEs, and degrees of freedom; p-values test treatment differences rather than
whether an individual biomass mean differs from zero.

# Check model assumptions

Variance components quantify the remaining between-whole-plot and residual
variation **after accounting for the fixed effects**. They do not measure the
amount of biomass variation caused by termination method. The plots assess
residual spread and approximate normality; they do not prove the assumptions.

```{r variance-summary}
variance_table <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(biomass_model)) |>
  transmute(
    component = grp,
    variance = vcov,
    SD = sdcor
  )

show_table(
  variance_table,
  "Variance components for soybean biomass (kg/ha)",
  digits = 1
)

cat(
  "Singular fit:",
  lme4::isSingular(biomass_model, tol = 1e-4),
  "\n"
)

diag_data <- biomass_data |>
  mutate(
    fitted = fitted(biomass_model),
    residual = residuals(biomass_model)
  )
```

```{r residual-diagnostics, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
ggplot(diag_data, aes(fitted, residual, color = site_year)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    x = "Fitted soybean biomass (kg/ha)",
    y = "Residual (kg/ha)",
    color = "Site-year"
  )

ggplot(diag_data, aes(sample = residual)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Theoretical normal quantile",
    y = "Residual quantile"
  )

ggplot(diag_data, aes(site_year, residual, color = treatment)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0, seed = 123),
    size = 2.5
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = treatment_colors) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = experiment_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Residual (kg/ha)",
    color = "Management system"
  )
```
# Test management system, site-year, and their interaction

Type III tests use Satterthwaite degrees of freedom with sum contrasts. The
management-system test addresses mean differences averaged over the three
site-years; the interaction assesses evidence that those differences vary
across site-years.

```{r model-anova}
biomass_anova <- anova(
  biomass_model,
  type = 3,
  ddf = "Satterthwaite"
)

show_table(
  as.data.frame(biomass_anova) |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("term"),
  "Type III ANOVA for soybean biomass",
  digits = 3
)

readr::write_csv(as.data.frame(biomass_anova) |> tibble::rownames_to_column("term"),
                 file.path(tab_dir, "primary_model_anova.csv"))
```
The management-system test gave F =
`r formatC(biomass_anova["treatment", "F value"], format = "f", digits = 3)`
(p `r fmt_p(biomass_anova["treatment", "Pr(>F)"])`), and the site-year test gave F =
`r formatC(biomass_anova["site_year", "F value"], format = "f", digits = 3)`
(p `r fmt_p(biomass_anova["site_year", "Pr(>F)"])`). The interaction gave F =
`r formatC(biomass_anova["treatment:site_year", "F value"], format = "f", digits = 3)`
(p `r fmt_p(biomass_anova["treatment:site_year", "Pr(>F)"])`).
A nonsignificant interaction does not establish identical system effects.
The interaction remains in the model regardless of this test.

# Estimated marginal means

Model-based means average the three site-years equally. Because the design is
balanced, these may coincide closely with the observed treatment means.
Model-based SEs reflect the covariance structure and should not be confused
with the descriptive SEs calculated from raw subplot observations.

```{r estimated-means}
biomass_emm <- simple_emm

biomass_emm_table <- as.data.frame(summary(biomass_emm)) |>
  select(treatment, emmean, SE, df, lower.CL, upper.CL)

show_table(
  biomass_emm_table,
  "Estimated marginal mean soybean biomass by management system (kg/ha)",
  digits = 1
)

readr::write_csv(biomass_emm_table,
                 file.path(tab_dir, "treatment_model_means.csv"))
```
The following estimates retain the interaction and describe each site-year
separately. SEs come from the primary common-variance mixed model. No additional
site-year-specific pairwise tests are introduced.

```{r site-year-treatment-means}
biomass_cell_emm <- emmeans(biomass_model, ~ treatment | site_year)
biomass_cell_table <- as.data.frame(summary(biomass_cell_emm)) |>
  mutate(site_year = unname(experiment_labels[as.character(site_year)]),
         `Estimated mean ± SE (kg/ha)` = sprintf("%.0f ± %.0f", emmean, SE)) |>
  select(site_year, treatment, `Estimated mean ± SE (kg/ha)`) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = `Estimated mean ± SE (kg/ha)`)
show_table(biomass_cell_table, "Model-estimated treatment means ± SE within site-year (kg/ha)")

readr::write_csv(as.data.frame(summary(biomass_cell_emm)),
                 file.path(tab_dir, "site_year_treatment_model_means.csv"))
```

# Compare management systems

Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons provide a family-wise error-controlled
reference for all ten comparisons among five management systems.
The split-plot model gives different standard errors for within-termination
and across-termination comparisons: whole-plot variation cancels from a
within-method difference but contributes to an across-method difference.
All comparisons describe implemented management systems; they do not isolate
termination method from supplemental management in a fully crossed factorial.

```{r treatment-comparisons}
biomass_pairs <- pairs(
  biomass_emm,
  adjust = "tukey"
)

biomass_pairs_table <- as.data.frame(summary(biomass_pairs)) |>
  select(contrast, estimate, SE, df, t.ratio, p.value)

show_table(
  biomass_pairs_table,
  "Pairwise comparisons among soybean management systems (kg/ha)",
  digits = 3
)

readr::write_csv(biomass_pairs_table,
                 file.path(tab_dir, "treatment_comparisons_tukey.csv"))
```

The targeted contrasts compare supplemental management options within the
same termination method. Holm adjustment is applied to this four-contrast
family. These contrasts avoid conflating different termination methods with
supplemental weed management.

```{r within-method-comparisons}
within_method <- contrast(
  biomass_emm,
  method = list(
    "TIM - TIC" = c(0, 0, 0, 1, -1),
    "RIM - RIC" = c(0, 1, -1, 0, 0),
    "RNO - RIM" = c(1, -1, 0, 0, 0),
    "RNO - RIC" = c(1, 0, -1, 0, 0)
  )
)

show_table(
  as.data.frame(summary(within_method, adjust = "holm")) |>
    select(contrast, estimate, SE, df, t.ratio, p.value),
  "Within-termination management comparisons (kg/ha)",
  digits = 3
)

readr::write_csv(as.data.frame(summary(within_method, adjust = "holm")) |>
                   select(contrast, estimate, SE, df, t.ratio, p.value),
                 file.path(tab_dir, "within_method_comparisons_holm.csv"))
```
# Fisher's LSD and letter groups

Unadjusted Fisher's LSD comparisons are reported for continuity with the
laboratory's established reporting practice. The overall management-system
ANOVA is the protection step for the current LSD interpretation; however,
*protected* LSD still does not provide the
same family-wise error control as Tukey across ten pairwise comparisons.
The corresponding compact letter display (CLD) assigns `a` to the highest
estimated mean. The code computes unadjusted comparisons regardless of the
omnibus p-value; if that test ceases to be significant after a data change,
revisit the protected-LSD interpretation. Contrast-specific SEs and degrees of
freedom are used, rather than a single universal LSD cutoff. Shared letters indicate that a difference was not detected
at the chosen threshold, **not** that treatments are equivalent.

```{r crop-biomass-fisher-lsd}
# Fisher's LSD: unadjusted pairwise comparisons.
crop_biomass_lsd <- pairs(biomass_emm, adjust = "none")

show_table(
  as.data.frame(summary(crop_biomass_lsd)) |>
    select(contrast, estimate, SE, df, t.ratio, p.value),
  "Fisher's LSD comparisons among management systems (kg/ha)",
  digits = 3
)

# Compact letter display, ordered from highest to lowest biomass.
crop_biomass_cld <- multcomp::cld(
  biomass_emm,
  adjust = "none",
  Letters = letters,
  sort = TRUE,
  reversed = TRUE
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    .group = gsub("\\s+", "", .group),
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = treatment_levels)
  )

show_table(
  crop_biomass_cld |>
    select(treatment, emmean, SE, .group),
  "Fisher's LSD groupings for soybean crop biomass",
  digits = 1
)

readr::write_csv(as.data.frame(summary(crop_biomass_lsd)) |>
                   select(contrast, estimate, SE, df, t.ratio, p.value),
                 file.path(tab_dir, "treatment_comparisons_fisher_lsd.csv"))
```
# Model-estimated biomass figures

The first figure shows management-system estimated marginal means with
model-based SEs and model-derived Fisher's LSD groupings. Its error bars
reflect precision under the fitted model, not the observed within-treatment
spread. The interaction remains in the model when means are averaged over
site-years.

```{r crop-biomass-treatment-figure, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
crop_biomass_treatment_data <- crop_biomass_cld |>
  mutate(label_y = emmean + SE + 250)

crop_biomass_treatment_fig <- ggplot(
  crop_biomass_treatment_data,
  aes(x = treatment, y = emmean, fill = treatment)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = emmean - SE, ymax = emmean + SE),
    width = 0.15,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(y = label_y, label = .group),
    size = 6,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = treatment_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = treatment_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Management system",
    y = "Soybean crop biomass (kg/ha)",
    caption = paste("Model-estimated means, averaged equally across site-years; error bars: ±1 model-based SE.",
                    lsd_caption, sep = "\n")
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16) + figure_caption_theme

crop_biomass_treatment_fig

dir.create(here("figures", "soybean_crop_biomass"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
ggsave(
  here("figures", "soybean_crop_biomass", "treatment_model.png"),
  plot = crop_biomass_treatment_fig,
  width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white"
)
```

# Alternative figures: observed means and descriptive SEs

These figures show arithmetic means and descriptive SEs calculated from the
observations. They reuse the **model-derived** Fisher's LSD letters rather
than testing differences using raw SEs. The error bars and letters thus
represent different quantities. For a given management system, the 12
observations come from distinct whole plots across three site-years. Its descriptive SE pools site-year differences
with within-site-year variation and does not represent the precision of an
equally weighted, site-year-adjusted treatment mean.

```{r crop-biomass-treatment-raw-figure, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
crop_biomass_treatment_raw <- biomass_data |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_biomass = mean(bean_biomass_kg_ha),
    sd_biomass = sd(bean_biomass_kg_ha),
    se_biomass = sd_biomass / sqrt(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    crop_biomass_cld |>
      select(treatment, .group),
    by = "treatment"
  ) |>
  mutate(label_y = mean_biomass + se_biomass + 250)

crop_biomass_treatment_raw_fig <- ggplot(
  crop_biomass_treatment_raw,
  aes(x = treatment, y = mean_biomass, fill = treatment)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = mean_biomass - se_biomass,
      ymax = mean_biomass + se_biomass
    ),
    width = 0.15,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(y = label_y, label = .group),
    size = 6
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = treatment_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = treatment_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Management system",
    y = "Soybean crop biomass (kg/ha)",
    caption = paste("Observed arithmetic means; error bars: ±1 descriptive SE (SD/√12), pooling site-years.",
                    "Letters compare model-estimated means averaged equally across site-years.",
                    lsd_caption, sep = "\n")
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16) + figure_caption_theme

crop_biomass_treatment_raw_fig

ggsave(
  here("figures", "soybean_crop_biomass", "treatment_raw.png"),
  plot = crop_biomass_treatment_raw_fig,
  width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white"
)
```
# Site-year comparisons

Site-year estimated marginal means average equally across the five management
systems. Fisher's LSD letters summarize model-based comparisons among the
three experiments; these should be understood as comparisons among the
observed site-years rather than an isolated causal effect of calendar year.

```{r crop-biomass-site-year-figure, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
crop_biomass_year_emm <- emmeans(
  biomass_model,
  ~ site_year,
  weights = "equal"
)

crop_biomass_year_lsd <- pairs(
  crop_biomass_year_emm,
  adjust = "none"
)

show_table(
  as.data.frame(summary(crop_biomass_year_lsd)) |>
    select(contrast, estimate, SE, df, t.ratio, p.value),
  "Fisher's LSD comparisons among site-years (kg/ha)",
  digits = 3
)

crop_biomass_year_data <- multcomp::cld(
  crop_biomass_year_emm,
  adjust = "none",
  Letters = letters,
  sort = TRUE,
  reversed = TRUE
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    site_year = factor(site_year, levels = names(experiment_labels)),
    .group = gsub("\\s+", "", .group),
    label_y = emmean + SE + 250
  )

crop_biomass_year_fig <- ggplot(
  crop_biomass_year_data,

) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = emmean - SE, ymax = emmean + SE),
    width = 0.15,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(y = label_y, label = .group),
    size = 6
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = experiment_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = experiment_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_comma(),
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Site-year",
    y = "Soybean crop biomass (kg/ha)",
    caption = paste("Model-estimated means, averaged equally across five systems; error bars: ±1 model-based SE.",
                    lsd_caption, sep = "\n")
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 16) + figure_caption_theme

crop_biomass_year_fig
```

# Results summary

Across the three observed site-years, soybean crop biomass differed among the
five management systems (p `r fmt_p(biomass_anova["treatment", "Pr(>F)"])`)
and among site-years (p `r fmt_p(biomass_anova["site_year", "Pr(>F)"])`).
There was no statistically significant treatment-by-site-year interaction
(p `r fmt_p(biomass_anova["treatment:site_year", "Pr(>F)"])`), but the model
retains it to estimate system means within individual site-years.

Estimated means were `r paste(paste0(as.character(biomass_emm_table$treatment), ": ", fmt_biomass(biomass_emm_table$emmean)), collapse = "; ")`
kg/ha. The tilled systems generally had higher biomass than the roller-crimped
systems. Fisher's LSD detected differences in
`r sum(as.data.frame(summary(crop_biomass_lsd))$p.value < 0.05)` of the ten
pairwise comparisons, covering all six tilled–rolled pairs. Tukey detected
`r sum(biomass_pairs_table$p.value < 0.05)` differences; it did not detect
TIM–RNO (p `r fmt_p(biomass_pairs_table$p.value[biomass_pairs_table$contrast == "RNO - TIM"])`)
or TIM–RIC (p `r fmt_p(biomass_pairs_table$p.value[biomass_pairs_table$contrast == "RIC - TIM"])`).
The figures' letters describe LSD rather than Tukey results. None of the four
within-termination supplemental-management comparisons was significant after
Holm adjustment (smallest p `r fmt_p(min(as.data.frame(summary(within_method, adjust = "holm"))$p.value))`).
These system comparisons do not isolate the causal contribution of termination
method because the five systems are not a fully crossed factorial.

Biomass was lower in 2023 Field V than in either 2024 experiment; the two 2024
site-years did not differ by LSD
(p `r fmt_p(as.data.frame(summary(crop_biomass_year_lsd))$p.value[3])`).
These are comparisons among observed experiments, not isolated effects of
calendar year. The 2023 RNO subplot that inadvertently received cultivation
limits interpretation of RNO versus RIC: the primary comparison estimates
differences by randomized assignment, including this implementation deviation.
No subplot has been reclassified.

Differences in soybean establishment, competition from living cereal rye,
planting conditions, and residue effects are possible explanations, not
mechanisms demonstrated by this biomass analysis. Greater crop biomass does
not necessarily imply greater grain yield; interpret these results alongside
establishment, weed biomass, and grain-yield analyses.

# Appendix: sensitivity to residual variance

The primary model assumes one residual variance across site-years. Conditional
residual plots assess spread and normality but do not prove these assumptions.
This check retains the treatment-by-site-year interaction and whole-plot random
intercept while allowing residual SD to differ among site-years. It does not
change treatment assignments or replace the primary model.

```{r residual-variance-sensitivity}
# Fit both versions with the same engine and fixed effects. Their REML
# likelihoods are comparable because only the covariance structure changes.
# Pass contrasts through nlme's argument, rather than factor attributes:
# this avoids contrast-attribute warnings when emmeans reconstructs its grid.
variance_data <- biomass_data
contrasts(variance_data$treatment) <- NULL
contrasts(variance_data$site_year) <- NULL
variance_equal <- nlme::lme(
  fixed = bean_biomass_kg_ha ~ treatment * site_year,
  random = ~ 1 | whole_plot_id,
  data = variance_data, method = "REML",
  contrasts = list(treatment = contr.sum(5), site_year = contr.sum(3))
)
variance_by_year <- nlme::lme(
  fixed = bean_biomass_kg_ha ~ treatment * site_year,
  random = ~ 1 | whole_plot_id,
  weights = nlme::varIdent(form = ~ 1 | site_year),
  data = variance_data, method = "REML",
  contrasts = list(treatment = contr.sum(5), site_year = contr.sum(3))
)
variance_comparison <- as.data.frame(anova(variance_equal, variance_by_year))
show_table(variance_comparison |>
             select(-call) |> tibble::rownames_to_column("model"),
           "Common versus site-year-specific residual variance (REML)", digits = 3)

residual_sd_ratios <- coef(variance_by_year$modelStruct$varStruct,
                          unconstrained = FALSE, allCoef = TRUE)
show_table(
  tibble(site_year = unname(experiment_labels[names(residual_sd_ratios)]),
         residual_SD_ratio = unname(residual_sd_ratios)),
  "Residual SD ratios relative to 2023 Field V", digits = 3
)

variance_equal_emm <- emmeans(variance_equal, ~ treatment, weights = "equal")
variance_year_emm <- emmeans(variance_by_year, ~ treatment, weights = "equal")
variance_sensitivity <- as.data.frame(summary(pairs(variance_equal_emm, adjust = "none"))) |>
  select(contrast, common_estimate = estimate, common_SE = SE,
         common_df = df, common_p = p.value) |>
  left_join(
    as.data.frame(summary(pairs(variance_year_emm, adjust = "none"))) |>
      select(contrast, unequal_estimate = estimate, unequal_SE = SE,
             unequal_df = df, unequal_p = p.value),
    by = "contrast"
  )
show_table(variance_sensitivity,
           "Pooled contrast sensitivity to residual variance (kg/ha; unadjusted p-values)",
           digits = 4)

# Pooled SEs can remain stable while site-year-specific precision changes.
variance_cell_se <- bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(emmeans(variance_equal, ~ treatment | site_year)) |>
    mutate(model = "Common residual variance"),
  as.data.frame(emmeans(variance_by_year, ~ treatment | site_year)) |>
    mutate(model = "Residual variance by site-year")
) |>
  group_by(site_year, model) |>
  summarise(min_SE = min(SE), max_SE = max(SE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(site_year = unname(experiment_labels[as.character(site_year)]))
show_table(variance_cell_se, "Range of treatment-mean SEs within each site-year (kg/ha)")
```

The residual-variance comparison gave p
`r fmt_p(variance_comparison[["p-value"]][2])`; AIC was
`r formatC(AIC(variance_equal), format = "f", digits = 2)` for common variance
and `r formatC(AIC(variance_by_year), format = "f", digits = 2)` for unequal variance.
There were `r sum((variance_sensitivity$common_p < 0.05) != (variance_sensitivity$unequal_p < 0.05))`
changed pooled LSD decisions between these two sensitivity fits. Their
unadjusted p-values use nlme/emmeans containment degrees of freedom rather than
the primary model's Satterthwaite approximation; compare covariance assumptions
within this pair of fits rather than attributing every difference from the
primary analysis to unequal variance.

These data provide limited evidence for different residual variances and no
compelling reason to replace the primary common-variance model. This does not
establish equal variances. Pooled comparisons can be stable while uncertainty
within individual site-years changes, as the SE table shows. No additional
site-year-specific pairwise comparisons are performed.

# Reproducibility and remaining limitations

The processed-data checks preserve one originally labeled treatment per block;
they cannot independently establish the randomized identity of the affected
2023 subplot without its field record. Any discrepancy with that record should
be flagged before analysis, not corrected by silently changing treatment labels.
The operations error does not change the whole-plot grouping. Interpret RNO–RIC
comparisons with the implementation deviation in mind.

The analysis uses the processed RDS directly. Packages include tidyverse,
here, conflicted, WrensBookshelf, lmerTest/lme4, emmeans, multcomp, multcompView,
nlme, knitr, and rmarkdown; the session below records their environment. Render
from the repository with these dependencies installed. Four final PNGs are
exported to `figures/` using the existing filenames and dimensions.

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```
